terms.comment: Tree names are mostly feminine, even in the second declension; rubus is masculine.

phrases.latin: quercūs, tiliae, fraxinī, salicēs rīvō imminentēs, jūglandēs, corylī, cornī
phrases.english: oaks, limes, ashes, willows overhanging the stream, walnuts, hazels, cornelian cherries

phrases.latin: Duae arborēs ibi stant etiam nunc, quercus et tilia, truncīs vīcīnīs, rāmīs jūnctīs.
phrases.english: Two trees stand there even now, an oak and a lime, their trunks side by side, their branches joined (Baucis and Philemon).

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
